input_signals.name: GrossProfitAmongLossMakers
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Within the population of loss-making firms, gross profitability separates firms whose losses come from overhead, interest, or transitory charges (which mean-revert) from firms whose product economics are broken; the market treats all reported losses alike, so high-gross-margin loss makers are underpriced and low-gross-margin loss makers overpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the signed z-score with a non-negative RANK of pretax-loss intensity removes the perverse short leg: profitable firms now receive a weight near zero and sit in the middle of the sort, so the spread is formed inside the distressed subsample rather than against the profitability premium. The long leg is high-gross-margin loss makers and the short leg is loss makers with weak or negative gross margins, which is exactly the stated recovery-versus-failure discrimination.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitUnderNegativeWorkingCapital
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Negative working capital is a structural distress state in which current claims must be met from operating inflows; high gross profitability makes that structure self-financing and safe, whereas thin margins under a working-capital deficit imply a recurring funding gap met by dilutive financing.
input_signals.reasoning: Holding the centered gross-profit quality leg fixed and swapping the conditioner from bottom-line loss intensity to a balance-sheet liquidity gap isolates which distress dimension carries the mispricing — an income-statement state or a funding-structure state. Working capital is available for nearly all non-financial firms, so coverage should exceed the loss-conditioned versions and the sort composition should be more stable over time.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ChronicLossCountTimesGrossProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), 0), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent rather than transitory distress produces the deepest neglect and the tightest institutional constraints, so gross profitability should discriminate most sharply between recoverable and terminal firms among habitual loss makers.
input_signals.reasoning: Using the raw 0-5 loss-year count instead of its cross-sectional RANK implements the neutralization the hypothesis requires: never-loss firms receive an exact zero weight rather than a mid-range tie, so the spread is formed strictly inside the chronically distressed population and its intensity scales with the number of loss years. This makes the chronic-versus-transitory test clean when compared with the accepted loss-intensity-conditioned signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), ts_sum( indicator( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), 0 ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitUnderNetDebt
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability is the resource that services claims, so its pricing error should be largest where claims are largest net of cash; among heavily net-indebted firms, high gross margin means solvency is not really at risk while thin margin means the debt cannot be earned out.
input_signals.reasoning: This holds the successful centered gross-profit quality leg fixed and swaps the conditioner from a working-capital deficit to net-of-cash leverage, isolating which distress dimension carries the mispricing rather than restating the winner. Because gen-1 showed that *uncentered* coverage levels conditioned on net debt earn negative FF5 alpha, a positive result here would establish that centering the quality leg — not the choice of distress variable — was the decisive fix.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( lt, che ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: IndustryNeutralGrossProfitUnderWorkingCapitalDeficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The gross-profit-in-distress premium reflects firm-specific survival capacity, not industry-level margin structure; measuring gross profitability relative to industry peers should therefore purify the signal and reduce the profitability-factor loading that suppresses FF5 alpha.
input_signals.reasoning: The critic's main risk for the archive's best joint signal is RMW spanning, since raw gross profitability is highly correlated with the profitability factor; industry-demeaning removes the sector-margin component (retail versus software) that drives most of that correlation while preserving the within-industry quality-versus-distress contrast. Comparing this with the accepted raw-ZSCORE version isolates exactly how much of the alpha is industry composition rather than firm-level distress discrimination.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitAfterLiquidityDeterioration
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, at), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A sharp deterioration in working capital creates a fresh, unfunded financing need; gross profitability determines whether that gap is self-funded from operations or must be closed through distressed borrowing or dilution, so the quality discrimination should be strongest immediately after liquidity worsens.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than blending two untested conditioners into an averaged weight, this substitutes the *flow* of the working-capital state for its *level*, which is a substantive timing hypothesis: the archive shows gross profit interacts with a standing working-capital deficit, and the open question is whether the mispricing arises when the deficit is chronic or when it newly appears. The conditioning weight remains a bounded non-negative rank of deterioration so firms with improving liquidity sit in the middle of the sort, and requiring only two annual observations keeps coverage close to the accepted level-based version.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( wcap, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitAtOwnLiquidityTrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distress is firm-specific: a working-capital position sitting at its own five-year low signals that the firm has exhausted its customary liquidity slack, and it is in that state that gross profitability determines whether the trough is temporary or terminal.
input_signals.reasoning: All archived conditioners are cross-sectional (levels or one-year changes relative to peers), whereas this one is within-firm, which matters because a retailer's normal negative working capital is not distress while the same level would be for a capital-goods maker. If the own-history conditioner outperforms the cross-sectional deficit level, it means the mispricing follows firm-specific liquidity exhaustion rather than industry funding structure, which also sharpens the interpretation of the industry-neutral result from gen 3.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: AssetTurnoverUnderWorkingCapitalDeficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(revt, at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-profit-to-assets is the product of margin and asset turnover, and for a firm funding itself from a negative working-capital position it is turnover — the speed at which assets convert into collectible sales — that determines whether current claims can be met from operations.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than swapping conditioners on a leg that already failed, this decomposes the archive's best-performing quality leg into its DuPont components and tests the turnover half, which has never been used in this archive and is economically the cash-cycle channel most relevant to working-capital distress. If turnover carries the interaction, the mechanism is cash-conversion speed rather than pricing power, which would redirect the remaining generations away from margin-based quality measures and toward velocity-based ones.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( revt, at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerAndCashBackingAtLiquidityTrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), revt)))), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm at its own liquidity trough survives on two distinct resources: the margin it earns on sales and the fraction of reported profit that arrives as cash. Firms strong on both are the most underpriced in that state; firms with thin margins and accrual-inflated earnings are the most likely to require distressed financing.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has cleanly separated its two productive quality channels — gross profitability supplies the reliable Fama-MacBeth slopes while cash backing of earnings supplies the largest FF5 alpha — and they have never been combined, so this is the natural consolidation rather than a rank-averaging duplicate. Crucially the conditioner is a *level* state (distance from the firm's own five-year working-capital minimum), so the earlier contradiction of using a working-capital decline as both good and bad is avoided.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( sumrank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), revt ) ) ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: IndustryNeutralGrossProfitAtLiquidityTrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Both the quality measurement and the distress measurement should be firm-specific rather than structural: margins relative to industry peers and liquidity relative to the firm's own history isolate genuine survival discrimination from sector-level margin and funding conventions.
input_signals.reasoning: Industry-demeaning the quality leg raised the cross-sectional t-stat from 3.49 to 4.68 while preserving alpha, and the own-history trough conditioner produced the archive's best Sharpe, so crossing the two independently validated design choices is the highest-probability route to joint strength. Because both legs are relative measures, the resulting portfolio should carry less RMW and industry loading than any archived variant, which is where the FF5 alpha of the level-based signals was leaking.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashEarningsToAssetsAtLiquidityTrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What the market misprices among liquidity-exhausted firms is cash earning power per unit of capital; pre-depreciation earnings on assets measure the cash the asset base actually throws off, which is the resource that funds survival.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates whether the archive's success comes from gross profit specifically or from asset-scaled profitability in general — the decisive question raised by the failure of every per-sales leg — by holding the winning trough conditioner fixed and substituting cash earnings on assets for gross profit on assets. Cash earnings sit further down the income statement and include overhead and interest, so a strong result would mean the mispriced quantity is bottom-line cash generation rather than product-level margin power.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitDuringCashDrawdown
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Drawing down the cash stock is the most visible sign that internal funding is being consumed; among firms actively burning cash, earning power determines whether the drawdown is a temporary investment phase or the start of a financing spiral.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested the cash *level* as a conditioner (repeatedly weak) but never the cash *drawdown*, and the working-capital results suggest it is liquidity dynamics rather than liquidity levels that identify the constrained subsample. Because cash and working capital are distinct funding pools, a positive result would show the mechanism generalises across liquidity sources rather than being specific to operating working capital, which is the main external-validity concern for the archive's leaders.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderChronicWorkingCapitalDeficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), 0), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that has operated with negative working capital in several of the past five years has a structural, not episodic, dependence on operating inflows and on supplier forbearance; earning power is the only thing that makes that structure sustainable, so it should discriminate returns most strongly there.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not an average of the archive's conditioners: it converts the distress state from a cross-sectional level or a within-firm extremum into a persistence count, which assigns an exact zero to every firm that has never run a deficit and therefore forms the spread strictly inside the structurally constrained population. It also answers a question the archive has posed but never resolved on the balance-sheet side — whether chronic or transitory constraint carries the mispricing — with the count construction that previously worked for losses (fmb 2.56) rather than the rank construction that diluted it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), ts_sum( indicator( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), 0 ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerDuringNonCashCurrentAssetBloat
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A rise in non-cash current assets per dollar of sales means inventory is not selling and receivables are not collecting; this asset-side bloat is an early warning of demand deterioration, and earning power determines whether the firm can absorb the resulting cash absorption or must finance it externally.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's conditioners all use net working capital, which offsets inventory and receivable buildup against payables and therefore mixes a demand problem with a supplier-credit decision; isolating the non-cash current-asset side is an economically distinct distress signal and is the mirror image of the payables-driven funding channel. Since it is a per-sales flow of an asset-side item conditioned on an asset-scaled quality leg, it cannot be reproduced by rescaling any existing entry, and both inputs are widely reported so coverage should stay near 0.12.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderOperatingCashAbsorption
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), lct), revt), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically correct measure of operating funding stress is the change in *non-cash* working capital per dollar of sales, since that is the amount of cash the operating cycle absorbed; firms absorbing cash into inventory and receivables face a funding need whose resolution depends on their earning power.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's conditioners each capture a fragment of this quantity — total working-capital change confounds it with the cash balance, and the non-cash current-asset version ignores the payables offset that finances the buildup — so this is a unification into the standard cash-flow-statement construct rather than an average of prior signals. If it beats both parents, the mechanism is genuinely operating-cash absorption; if it does not, the archive's alphas are driven by the cash-balance component and later work should say so explicitly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( sub( act, che ), lct ), revt ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderConjunctiveLiquidityStress
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, at), 1)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Only firms that are simultaneously deteriorating and at the bottom of their own liquidity range are genuinely constrained; either condition alone is common and often benign, so the earning-power discrimination should be concentrated where both hold.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a conjunction, not the arithmetic blend previously flagged: MIN assigns a weight near zero unless a firm is stressed on *both* the flow and the own-history state, so the resulting portfolio is a strict subset of each parent's long and short legs rather than a diversified average of them. The economic claim being tested — that the two conditions are jointly necessary — is falsifiable and cannot be inferred from the parents, whose weights each admit large numbers of one-dimensionally stressed firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), min( rank( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( wcap, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerImprovementAtLiquidityTrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: For a firm at its own liquidity trough, the informative quantity is whether earning power on assets is rising or falling: an improving return on the asset base means the squeeze will be outgrown, while a deteriorating one means the trough is the start of a spiral.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived quality leg conditioned on a liquidity state is a level; the only change-based quality leg tested was a per-sales margin change among loss makers, and per-sales scaling has since been shown to be the wrong deflator, so the level-versus-change question remains open for the deflator that actually works. A positive result would identify a distinct, cheap-to-update timing channel that is naturally orthogonal to the profitability factor because it is a first difference.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerWithExhaustedInternalCapital
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(ADD(re, che), at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Accumulated retained earnings plus cash measures the stock of internal capital a firm has built up; when that stock is exhausted the firm depends entirely on current operations and external markets, and earning power determines which of those two it can rely on.
input_signals.reasoning: All archived conditioners are short-horizon liquidity flows or one-year states, whereas this is a cumulative history-of-solvency stock — the Altman retained-earnings channel augmented with the liquid buffer — so it identifies a different constrained population (long-term loss accumulators rather than firms in a current squeeze). Because it uses only balance-sheet stocks it is available for nearly all firms and should give the batch's highest coverage, providing a robustness check on whether the mechanism needs flow information at all.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( add( re, che ), at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerDuringOperatingAssetContraction
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(GROWTH(SUB(at, che), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A shrinking operating asset base signals retrenchment — plant closures, receivable factoring, inventory liquidation — and among such firms earning power separates deliberate downsizing toward a profitable core from forced liquidation of a failing one.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the liability-side certification story, whose measure was confounded by cash drawdown, in favour of an asset-side distress state that no archive entry uses: every existing conditioner is a liquidity flow, stock, or own-history state, whereas contraction of non-cash assets identifies firms actively divesting productive capacity. Netting cash out of the asset base is essential here because cash swings would otherwise masquerade as capacity divestment, and the conditioner remains a bounded non-negative rank so growing firms sit in the middle of the sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( growth( sub( at, che ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderWorkingCapitalInstability
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(ABS(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, at), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating liquidity position moves sharply in either direction are the firms whose funding needs are least predictable; their survival prospects depend most on earning power, and the market's slow processing of that dependence is what generates the abnormal return.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly tests the archive's unresolved sign symmetry: if the absolute magnitude of the working-capital change subsumes both the deterioration conditioner and the absorption/bloat conditioner, then the mechanism is constraint sensitivity rather than the direction of the liquidity move, which would reinterpret four archived signals with one construct. The measure needs only two annual observations, so coverage should exceed the trough-based variants while the conditioner remains a bounded non-negative rank that leaves stable-working-capital firms in the middle of the sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( abs( delta( ratio( wcap, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderStockAndFlowDistress
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(ADD(re, che), at)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, at), 1)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is genuinely constrained when it has both exhausted its accumulated internal capital and is currently losing operating liquidity; either alone can be benign, but together they leave earning power as the only remaining source of funds.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the gen-7 conjunction, whose two conditioners were both working-capital-derived and therefore largely redundant, this joins a cumulative solvency *stock* (retained earnings plus cash, fmb 3.95, coverage 0.143) with a current liquidity *flow* (the archive's highest-alpha conditioner), which are economically and statistically distinct. The product of two bounded ranks is a smooth conjunction that avoids the near-zero weight clustering of MIN, so decile composition should stay stable while the tails concentrate on doubly constrained firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), mul( rank( winsor( neg( ratio( add( re, che ), at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( delta( ratio( wcap, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerNetOfCapitalConsumptionAtTrough
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(SUB(RATIO(wcap, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The survival-relevant measure of earning power is what the asset base produces after replacing the capacity it consumes; subtracting depreciation from gross profit gives the sustainable operating surplus available to creditors and suppliers.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen 6 established that bottom-line cash earnings on assets destroys the alpha (+0.7%) while gross profit on assets preserves it (+4.5%), but that comparison confounds three cost blocks — depreciation, overhead, and interest — and this proposal isolates the first one, telling us precisely which line item carries the noise. That is a substantive attribution about the mispriced construct rather than a rescaling, and the answer determines whether the final generation should use gross profit or a capital-consumption-adjusted surplus.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( sub( ratio( wcap, at ), ts_min( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderChronicLiquidityVolatility
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(wcap, at), 5), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Chronic instability of the operating liquidity position, not a single year's swing, identifies firms whose funding requirements are structurally unpredictable; earning power should be priced most strongly in that group because it is the only reliable buffer against recurring cash shortfalls.
input_signals.reasoning: Paired with Signal 1, this separates transient from persistent liquidity instability, which is the cleanest way to interpret the archive's puzzling sign symmetry: if the five-year volatility conditioner performs as well as or better than the one-year absolute change, the mechanism is a stable firm characteristic rather than an event, and the final signal should use the persistent measure for portfolio stability. The volatility conditioner also has no directional interpretation at all, so it cannot be confounded with the accrual or investment channels that overlap the signed working-capital measures.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( vol( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderNearTermClaimPressure
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, che), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What forces a firm into distressed financing is the size of the claims falling due within the year relative to its asset base, net of the cash it can pay them with; earning power is the flow that must cover that gap, so it should be priced most strongly where near-term net claims are heaviest.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than smoothing an archived quality leg, this substitutes a maturity-weighted claims conditioner that the archive has never paired with gross profitability: total net debt (alpha +2.3%) mixes claims due in twenty years with claims due next quarter, and the only near-term measure tested previously (short-term debt net of cash) was paired with a per-sales quality leg now known to be the wrong deflator. Current liabilities net of cash is well-behaved with an asset denominator — no near-zero divisor problem — and is reported for essentially all firms, so coverage should be among the archive's highest.
input_signals.author: proposer

input_signals.name: EarningPowerAmongLeveredLossMakers
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Distance to default requires both a loss and creditors: a loss-making firm with no debt simply shrinks, while a levered profitable firm is safe, so it is the conjunction of loss severity and leverage that identifies firms where gross profitability decides whether the debt can be earned out.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the flagged construction by never dividing by debt: both components are asset-scaled and separately well-behaved, and the MIN conjunction gives a high weight only when the firm is simultaneously deeply loss-making and meaningfully levered, which is exactly the population the distance-to-default story requires and which the archive's asset-scaled loss conditioner (strong slope, near-zero alpha) failed to isolate. Low-leverage micro-caps with trivial losses now receive a weight near zero instead of dominating the tail, so the spread should be formed among firms that genuinely have creditors to fail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), min( rank( winsor( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerWhenUnstableAndLossMaking
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(wcap, at), 5), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: An unpredictable funding requirement is dangerous only when current earnings are not covering it; combining liquidity instability with a current pretax loss identifies firms that must fund an unpredictable gap out of nothing, and there earning power is decisive.
input_signals.reasoning: The two conditioners come from different financial statements and have opposite empirical profiles in this archive — loss intensity gives the strongest slopes but weak alphas, instability the strongest alphas — so their product tests whether the two metrics disagree because each captures half of the constrained population. Multiplying bounded ranks keeps the weight non-negative and smooth, so unstressed firms remain in the middle of the sort rather than forming an arbitrary zero mass.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), mul( rank( winsor( vol( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderPretaxIncomeInstability
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(pi, at), 5), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If the mechanism is uncertainty about the resources available to meet obligations, then instability of pretax income should condition the earning-power premium just as instability of working capital does; volatile bottom lines make external financing expensive and internal earning power valuable.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the cleanest generalisation test of the instability finding to a completely different measurement source — an income-statement second moment rather than a balance-sheet one — and it also distinguishes the mechanism from a pure working-capital or accrual story. It is not a rediscovery of the failed gen-1 volatility signal, where earnings stability was the *signed quality* leg (stability treated as good); here volatility is the non-negative distress weight, which is the opposite structural role and the one the archive has shown to work.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( vol( ratio( pi, at ), 5 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerAndCashBackingUnderLiquidityInstability
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))), RANK(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(wcap, at), 5), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms facing unpredictable funding needs are protected by both high earning power per unit of capital and earnings that arrive as cash rather than accruals; the two resources are complementary, and the combination should be priced most strongly where the funding requirement is least predictable.
input_signals.reasoning: The composite quality state delivered the archive's highest Fama-MacBeth t-stat and Sharpe ratio when paired with the trough conditioner, but its accrual leg was revenue-scaled — the deflator now known to fail — and it lost coverage; asset-scaling that leg and pairing it with the best-performing instability conditioner targets the strongest joint result available from validated components. This is a consolidation of two independently confirmed findings rather than a rank-average of archived signals, since neither the asset-scaled composite nor this pairing has been evaluated.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( sumrank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), neg( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) ) ), rank( winsor( vol( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderDemandUncertaintyAndDeficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(VOL(GROWTH(revt, 1), 5), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The deepest constraint arises when a firm must fund a structural working-capital deficit out of a volatile revenue stream: the deficit means claims come due continuously while demand uncertainty means the inflows to meet them are unreliable, so earning power is the only buffer.
input_signals.reasoning: This traces the instability mechanism to its economic origin — uncertainty in the sales process rather than in the balance-sheet residual — and combines it with the structural funding state, so it tests whether working-capital volatility has been proxying for demand volatility all along. Because the uncertainty measure is a revenue growth moment and the state measure is a balance-sheet level, the conjunction is not reconstructible from any archived conditioner.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), mul( rank( winsor( vol( growth( revt, 1 ), 5 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderRecurringCashDepletion
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1)), 0), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Fragility shows up as the frequency with which a firm depletes its cash buffer, not the magnitude of its balance-sheet swings; a firm that has drawn down cash in most of the past five years is chronically unable to self-fund, and earning power decides whether the pattern ends in recovery or insolvency.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces an operator-level variant with an economically and statistically different conditioner: an episode count is scale-free and outlier-insensitive, which directly answers the objection that the leading volatility conditioner is a size and idiosyncratic-risk proxy, since a frequency cannot load on the magnitude of a firm's balance sheet. It also assigns an exact zero to firms that never depleted cash, so the spread is formed strictly among firms with a demonstrated history of recurring internal-funding shortfalls rather than among firms that merely have variable accounts.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), ts_sum( indicator( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ), 0 ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: EarningPowerUnderMaturityMismatchedInstability
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(wcap, at), 5), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Unpredictable operating funding needs become dangerous only when they are financed with claims that must be rolled within the year; the conjunction of liquidity instability and short-term debt net of cash is a genuine maturity mismatch, and there earning power determines whether the roll succeeds.
input_signals.reasoning: Instead of multiplying two moments of the same working-capital variable, this pairs the instability conditioner with an independent liability-structure dimension, so the interaction expresses a mismatch between the timing of funding needs and the timing of obligations rather than a rescaled version of one variable. It also rehabilitates the rollover dimension whose earlier failure (alpha −5.2%) is now attributable to its per-sales quality leg, a deflator since shown to fail throughout the archive, while the asset-scaled dlc−che construct avoids the near-zero denominators that broke the earlier default-proximity attempt.
